about: Shared cases for the observer's three text rules, read by tests/test_observer_text.c (the C in src/llm/observer_text.c) and tests/test_observer_rules.py (the Python in tools/observer_sentence_pairs.py, tools/observer_plant.py and tools/observer_judge_score.py). Each side must give every expected value. Divergences found 2026-11-15 and how each was resolved: journal/audit004-observer.md, item 2.

sentences.text: He met Mr. Darcy. Then J. K. Rowling wrote. It was 1866. So.
sentences.why: a title and initials end nothing; a digit before the period does

sentences.text: St. Ives is far. Dr. Watson came. Capt. Powell rode.
I saw Mr. X. Then I left.
want: I saw Mr. X. Then I left.
sentences.why: a single capital is an initial even when it ends a sentence (known limit)
closing curly quote, then a capital
a lower-case word after the quote: no boundary

sentences.text: The end.' He laughed. "Go." Then (Aside.) More.
sentences.why: straight quotes and a bracket close; an opening quote or bracket may precede the capital

sentences.text: my machine and Kantos Kan’s. Making his way

a title after a dash and an opening quote

sentences.text: He paused—then went on. Dash ends.—Then more.
sentences.why: an em dash is no space: no boundary straight after a period

sentences.text: Zoë left. Émile stayed. Then Zoë came.
sentences.why: an accented capital starts no sentence (ASCII capitals only, known limit)

sentences.text: Wait... What now? It cost 5. Then 6 more.

leading spaces belong to no sentence (the Python kept them until 2026-11-15)

sentences.text: Ends here. Next starts. Then	Tab.	After tab.
sentences.why: only a space or a tab separates sentences; a no-break space does not (the Python split there until 2026-11-15)
